name: Facet
text: Adopt a dark theme by default, switching to light only if the user manually overrides it. Dark themes reduce eye strain in low light and match the competitive analysis findings—users expect this for data tools. The trade-off is slightly lower text readability in bright rooms, but we prioritize comfort for long sessions. After 30 days of no override, we lock the dark theme to reinforce consistency.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t preference—it’s habituation. Users who override once won’t revisit settings, locking themselves into a mode that may not suit their task. Instead, let the theme match the *task*: default to dark for analysis-heavy work, light for presentation or editing, and auto-switch based on time or app focus. Settle it with A/B tests measuring completion speed and error rates in both modes.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Auto-switching by time or ambient light trades *one* habituation risk for another—users will override the system once, then forget it’s there, ending up in the wrong theme for their task. Instead, let the *task* drive the theme: default dark for analysis, light for editing/presenting, with a persistent, visible toggle that logs overrides to prove habituation isn’t the default.
